snapshots.name: Katherina
snapshots.body: Baptista's elder daughter, known throughout Padua for her sharp tongue and short temper, which have earned her the label of shrew. Her father will not allow her younger sister to marry until Katherina herself is wed.

snapshots.name: Petruchio
snapshots.body: A gentleman of Verona who arrives in Padua chiefly in search of a wealthy wife, undeterred by Katherina's reputation. He sets about courting her with a brashness that matches her own temper.

snapshots.name: Bianca
snapshots.body: Baptista's younger daughter, admired throughout Padua for her sweetness and courted by several suitors at once. Her father's condition, that Katherina marry first, is the engine behind much of the play's scheming.

snapshots.name: Lucentio
snapshots.body: A young gentleman newly arrived in Padua to study, who falls for Bianca at first sight and disguises himself as a tutor to win access to her. He swaps identities with his own servant Tranio to carry out the scheme.

snapshots.name: Baptista
snapshots.body: A wealthy Paduan gentleman and father to both Katherina and Bianca. He refuses to let Bianca marry until a husband is found for her more difficult elder sister.

snapshots.name: Hortensio
snapshots.body: A gentleman of Padua and one of Bianca's suitors, later a friend of Petruchio's. He disguises himself as a music tutor in his own effort to court Bianca.

snapshots.name: Tranio
snapshots.body: Lucentio's clever servant, who agrees to impersonate his master in public while Lucentio disguises himself to woo Bianca directly. He manages the resulting complications with considerable wit.

snapshots.name: Grumio
snapshots.body: Petruchio's long-suffering servant, who bears the brunt of his master's rough humor and short patience. His comic exchanges with Petruchio and others punctuate the courtship plot.

snapshots.name: Vincentio
snapshots.body: Lucentio's father, an elderly gentleman of Pisa, whose unexpected arrival in Padua threatens to unravel his son's elaborate disguise. His confusion at finding an impostor claiming his identity drives one of the play's broadest comic scenes.

snapshots.name: Gremio
snapshots.body: An elderly, wealthy suitor for Bianca's hand, rival to both Hortensio and the disguised Lucentio. His age and manner make him one of the play's more comic suitors.

snapshots.name: Biondello
snapshots.body: Lucentio's second servant, party to his master's scheme of disguises and swapped identities. He helps keep the plot's many deceptions coordinated.

snapshots.name: Curtis
snapshots.body: A servant at Petruchio's country house, who hears from Grumio just how roughly his new mistress Katherina has been received on the journey home. His scene offers an outside view of Petruchio's household before Katherina arrives.
